guidance: {"kind": "procedure_guidance_v2", "procedure": "Audit the next action using only supplied public evidence and the execution catalog. First extract the latest request target and operation in its own terms. Separate the target entity from contextual words such as job or work. Then recover any still-active originating request, continuation trigger, ordering revision and cancellation. A continuation can activate an earlier authorization without issuing a new request. Match the target entity and requested operation against the candidate catalog scope AND its prerequisites. Reject a candidate when its scope excludes the requested entity even if contextual words sound similar. Do not infer the task category merely from the word job. Correlate receipts with the exact submitted action and target; partial success does not discharge the remaining obligation. Before recommending termination or abstention, reconcile every live obligation against its latest correlated receipt: preserve still-live authorization, continuation, ordering revisions, cancellations, and conditional/pending work. Treat an explicit continuation as activating a retained obligation when its condition holds, but do not infer completion from scene similarity or a generic continuation. Match the requested entity and operation to the catalog scope and prerequisites; partial receipts leave the remainder pending, while a correlated native-complete receipt discharges only that exact obligation. Use compact Target, Authority, Match, Action fields; cite evidence IDs and state the strongest conflict or unmet prerequisite. The actor decides. Do not interpret missing recent mention as cancellation. In the recommendation use four compact labeled fields: Target (request entity/operation), Authority (origin or continuation evidence), Match (candidate scope and satisfied prerequisite), Action (one recommendation or abstain). In uncertainty name the strongest conflicting evidence or unmet prerequisite; do not invent one. Cite the supporting evidence IDs. Treat memory as fallible: prefer explicit public requests and correlated receipts over summary assertions. Never execute, veto, invent evidence, or use private evaluator information. The actor decides."}
update: {"kind": "procedure_update_v2", "procedure": "Consolidate public requests and correlated execution receipts into a compact obligation ledger in the existing memory text. Preserve for each live obligation: origin event, target, requested operation, activation or continuation condition, current ordering and revision event, status, and latest correlated receipt. Record conditional future work as authorized but waiting for its stated condition, not unauthorized. Distinguish authorization from readiness and completion. Carry forward the originating authorization and continuation trigger across unrelated intervening work. A short continuation request need not repeat the original authorization. Remove an obligation only on an explicit applicable cancellation or a receipt proving its requested extent complete. One successful segment leaves the remainder pending when the request requires more. A submitted action is only a commitment until the correlated receipt. A revision changes only its stated scope; retain the original ordering needed to resolve relative references. Before saving, check each previously pending or conditional obligation: either retain it with its trigger, or cite the cancellation/completion event that discharges it. Never turn an actor assumption about authorization into a user restriction. Preserve unresolved conflicts as uncertain. Within the shared memory budget prioritize live obligations and evidence IDs over coordinates or verbose completed-job descriptions; compact discharged jobs. Do not invent a plan, task, restriction, dependency or completion. History records the actual change and its evidence."}
